score.label: Change in the share of the population outside the founding pool
score.description: When an official census or statistical-office series can be mapped to the founding pool, the score is the change, in percentage points, in the share of the population outside that pool, from the earliest comparable official figure (around 1970 where possible) to the latest. Where no such series exists, the map falls back to the UN DESA 1990–2020 dissimilarity index (D) and labels the country as a UN migrant-origin estimate that understates change.

scale.note: Five bands cut to the distribution of the 25 census-based scores (signed change outside the founding pool). They are not the Crime tab’s 20-point steps, and they are not the v1 UN-D bands. Negative values mean the founding pool’s share rose.
scale.estimate_note: Hatched countries are coloured on a separate UN-D scale so they are never visually identical to a census score.

source.census: Official statistical-office census and population-register series compiled in the StopBias ethnic-pools global dataset v1.13.0 (23 November 2026).
source.un: UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024, used only where no usable official ethnicity, race, ancestry or migration-background series is available.
source.mapping: country_pool_map.csv (primary / founding pool and UN M49 subregion). Caucasus ethnic codes and the ARM/GEO origin rule: data/demographics/caucasus_ethnic_groups.json. primary_pool in this file is the country map.
source.world_context: UN DESA World Population Prospects 2024; geographic regions, not an ethnicity series.
source.notes_en: This file is provisional and is not a published finding. No scores were invented. Australia and Israel have official series that cannot be turned into a cross-pool founding-pool score without inventing a mapping, so they keep a UN-D fallback on the map and are labelled separately. Peru’s mother-tongue series is stored the same way, pending a ruling on whether a weak language-speaker proxy should be the headline (as Mexico already is). Indonesia (2010) and Zimbabwe (2022) are single census points with no change score. Fifteen country-to-pool assignments, and whether Nepal’s Tibeto-Burman groups and Laos’s Hmong count as East Asian, remain provisional and follow the existing project map (ethnic European pool; Turkey locked to the Middle East; South Africa scored on its ethnic European population). Georgia and Armenia are the Caucasus pool (CAU), separate from ethnic European and from the Semitic / Middle East and North Africa pool; that replaces their provisional ethnic European assignment. Azerbaijan stays in the Semitic / Middle East and North Africa pool. UN cross-pool foreign-born shares are recomputed from UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024 so that births in Georgia and Armenia count as Caucasus. Azerbaijan stays in the Semitic / Middle East and North Africa pool. The stored shares reproduce the previous ethnic European basis before that one change. South African origins stay Sub-Saharan African in that UN calculation, which is how those stored shares were built; South Africa's census score remains ethnic European.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.mapping_note: Scored founding population is ethnic European (White). Black African is the majority throughout the modern period and is recorded as the other pool (SSA). Afrikaner and English are the main White groups. Coloured (mixed) and the smaller Indian/South Asian minority are not the founding pool used for the score.
countries.un_source: UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024; Stats SA, South African Statistics 2002 tables 1.2-1.3; Census 2022 P0301.4 table 2.4; Census 2001 Primary Tables; Census 2011 Census in Brief tables 2.3-2.4
flags: over 20% of migrants of unknown origin in some year

census.metric_label: Change in the share of the population outside the founding pool, percentage points, earliest comparable official figure to the latest.
census.source: Stats SA, South African Statistics 2002 tables 1.2-1.3 (1946-1970, 1970 boundaries including TBVC, rounded to 1,000); Census 1996 and 2022 via Census 2022 P0301.4 table 2.4 (2022 excludes unspecified; full total 62,027,503); Census 2001 Primary Tables; Census 2011 Census in Brief tables 2.3-2.4
census.notes: No 1945 census. The 1946 Union census is the earliest population-group count. The series covers the full territory, with the TBVC homelands included, and excludes Namibia and Walvis Bay. The 1980, 1985 and 1991 censuses as published exclude the TBVC homelands and overstate the White share, so they are omitted. A 1991 model-adjusted White share of 13.4 (TBVC added back) and the 2026 mid-year estimate of 7.1 are context only and are not used as the latest figure. 1960 and 1970 African counts were sample-based. The White count rose from 2.37 million in 1946 to 4.50 million in 2022 while the White share fell from 20.8% to 7.3%. Counts (White / total): 1946 2,372,000/11,415,000; 1951 2,642,000/12,672,000; 1960 3,088,000/16,002,000; 1970 3,773,000/21,794,000; 1996 4,434,697/40,208,369; 2001 4,293,640/44,819,778; 2011 4,586,838/51,770,560; 2022 4,504,252/61,988,314 (2022 excludes unspecified; the full 2022 total is 62,027,503). Sources: Stats SA, South African Statistics 2002 tables 1.2-1.3 (1946-1970, 1970 boundaries including TBVC, rounded to 1,000); Census 1996 and 2022 via Census 2022 P0301.4 table 2.4; Census 2001 Primary Tables; Census 2011 Census in Brief tables 2.3-2.4. Drivers (Stats SA, Mid-year population estimates 2026, P0302, table 2, net international migration by population group): White net migration -99,574 (2001-06), -106,787 (2006-11), -111,346 (2011-16), -90,957 (2016-21), -94,898 (2021-26), total -503,562; Black African net migration +919,607 (2021-26), mostly from other Sub-Saharan countries, i.e. within SSA rather than into the scored ethnic European pool. The change in census shares therefore reflects differences in natural increase between groups plus net emigration of the White population, not cross-pool immigration (UN DESA cross-pool foreign-born share 0.5% in 2020).

census.notes: Shares of persons who stated a nationality (not-stated excluded: 1.0% of total 2002, 3.9% 2010, 11.3% 2021). EUR = Russians, Ukrainians, Belarusians, Germans; EAS = Kazakhs, Kyrgyz, Uzbeks (Turkic, per the project country map); MENA = Tajiks (per the project country map) + Jews (main Jewish line only; Mountain, Georgian and Central Asian Jews listed separately and left unmapped). unmapped = Tatars (3.9% 2002, 3.6% 2021 of those stating), Bashkirs, Chechens, Armenians, Azerbaijanis, other peoples of Russia and all others. CONCEPT BREAKS: (1) not-stated share rose sharply, much of it from administrative records with no nationality; (2) 2021 includes Crimea and Sevastopol, not covered in 2002/2010. D is on the stated-nationality basis. Caucasus assignment: Chechens, Armenians, Georgians and the other peoples coded CAU in data/demographics/caucasus_ethnic_groups.json are a separate pool from ethnic European and from Middle East and North Africa. In these rows they are inside unmapped, not inside EUR (EUR is Russians, Ukrainians, Belarusians and Germans only), so the ethnic European shares 83.7, 83.0 and 81.8 are not recast and no CAU share is invented. Azerbaijanis stay out of CAU; in these rows they also remain inside unmapped.

census.metric_label: Official statistical-office series stored for the country pop-up; not used as the map or ranked-list score.
census.source: BPS Statistics Indonesia: Kewarganegaraan, Suku Bangsa, Agama dan Bahasa Sehari-hari Penduduk Indonesia, Hasil Sensus Penduduk 2010 (2011), table 2 (via web archive of bps.go.id)
census.notes: Single census point (2010), so no change or D and no map score from this series. PAC = suku asal Papua (more than 466 Papuan groups, 1.14%); EAS = Cina (Chinese Indonesians, citizens, 1.20%); SEA = all other groups (Javanese 40.2%, Sundanese, Malay, Batak, Madurese, Maluku groups and others); unmapped = Asing/Luar Negeri (citizens of foreign origin, 0.07%). Base is 236,728,379 persons with an ethnicity classified, out of 237,641,326 enumerated. The map and ranked list keep the UN migrant-origin proxy.

census.metric_label: Change in the share of the population outside the founding pool, percentage points, earliest comparable official figure to the latest.
census.source: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics: 2009 Census ethnic affiliation table (knbs.or.ke/censusethnic.php, via web archive); 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Volume IV, table 2.31 Distribution of population by ethnicity/nationality
census.notes: EUR = Kenyan Europeans + European nationals; SAS = Kenyan Asians (citizens of South Asian origin by convention; KNBS label is Asian); MENA = Kenyan Arabs; unmapped = Kenyan (so stated, 1.6% in 2009, 0.4% in 2019), Kenyan Americans, non-Kenyan Asians (mixed origins), American, Caribbean and Oceania nationals, other nationality, stateless, not stated. SSA = all Kenyan African ethnic groups (Kenyan Somali, 2,780,502 in 2019, included: Horn of Africa sits in the SSA pool) plus East African and other African nationals, computed as the remainder of the total. The SSA rise is mostly the fall in the residual “Kenyan (so stated)” label. Shares to 2 decimals.
